trust_decision.summary: The FastAPI server decides what exception text goes into client-facing HTTP error bodies. Route handlers in lightrag/api/routers/* and lightrag_server.py copy str(e) verbatim into HTTPException(detail=...), so backend and storage error text (hosts, paths, SQL) reaches API clients.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'raw exception messages in API error responses'. A grep for detail=str(e) finds the query router first; it is the main user-facing endpoint.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: lightrag/api/routers/ollama_api.py:472 and lightrag/api/routers/ollama_api.py:747. Also an app-wide last-resort handler with no pinned-tree counterpart (fix.diff:75-86 in lightrag/api/lightrag_server.py create_app).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The Ollama-emulation router is a compatibility shim that copies Ollama's own error shape, and streaming error lines cannot become an HTTP 500 once the stream has started. The code says so explicitly at lightrag/api/routers/query_routes.py:866-871, so a solver can argue that the in-band NDJSON error is the designed protocol rather than a leak.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Client-actionable validation messages must still reach the client. The 422 chunking-config errors stay visible, only wrapped (fix.diff:13-20), and the graph edit/create/merge routes return 400 with detail=str(ve) for ValueError such as 'entity already exists'. An over-broad fix that blanks every detail, or turns every exception into a generic 500, breaks this client feedback. Also, HTTPException must not be swallowed by the new global handler (fix.diff:72-74).
